prerequisites: Basic elements of linear algebra and computer programming

learning_outcomes.text: Competence in writing mathematical models for optimization and decision problems
Competence in solving small applied PLC and PLI problems

syllabus_topics: Cycling and the Use of Bland's rule
Duality: dual variables and dual linear program
Understanding the dual problem: shadow costs
Cutting Plane Method (generalities and Gomory's cuts)
Branch and Bound Method (Generalities, searching strategies, B&B for knapsack problem, standard B&B for PLI)
Dynamic Programming (generalities, DP for knapsack 01, weight version and cost version, Bellman-Ford algorithm for Shortest Path Problem)

assessment_methods.method: Mathematical model design and implementation with GLPK
Linear programming and graph theory exercises

assessment_rules: The written examination consists of three parts: theory questions, mathematical model design, and numerical exercises. Part 1 is graded from -5 to 10 with a minimum score of 3. Parts 2 and 3 are graded up to 27. An optional oral questioning, which can be requested by the teacher or student, determines the final grade and can change the written exam grade by up to 4 points.
